title.narrative: Enhanced capacity for evidenced based macro-economic and employment policies and programmes

description.narrative:
The ILO’s support to Uganda focuses on enhancing the capacity for evidence-based macroeconomic and employment policies to promote full and productive employment. This initiative directly contributes to Uganda’s National Employment Policy (NEP), with a special emphasis on youth employment. Uganda has the youngest population globally, with over 800,000 young people entering the labor market each year, creating a significant challenge for employment creation. By partnering with the government and social partners, the ILO seeks to strengthen the policy and institutional frameworks that enable decent work, especially for young people and marginalized groups.
The strategy involves developing and implementing key national policies, such as the National Youth Policy and Plan, the Green Jobs and Skills Development Programme, and the National Apprenticeship Framework. These initiatives aim to foster inclusive economic growth, improve productivity, and address gender disparities in the labor market. Additionally, the ILO supports the government in finalizing and operationalizing the Employment Diagnostic Analysis (EDA) and promoting the integration of employment strategies into the National Development Plan (NDP II).
